findings.finding: The `git_base` refactor touches the execution primitive used by roughly 133 existing callers, but the plan does not explicitly require byte-for-byte preservation of the existing text-mode subprocess configuration and failure behavior. In particular, text-mode `stdout` and `stderr` decoding, environment, `cwd`, command argument construction, timeout cleanup/reaping, and `run_git_soft` behavior must remain unchanged. A generic `_popen_git(..., binary=...)` extraction can easily alter one of these incidentally.
findings.suggestion: Keep the shared execution path as small as possible and explicitly preserve the current `Popen`/`communicate` arguments in the text branch, including `encoding="utf-8"` and `errors="replace"` for every captured text stream. Add characterization tests for `stdout`, `stderr`, non-zero return codes, and the existing `run_git_soft` timeout behavior—not only `run_git` stdout decoding.

findings.finding: The timeout contract is stated for the bytes helper, but the implementation description only says it “maps `TimeoutExpired`.” A timed-out `Popen.communicate()` must also kill and reap the child process before returning. Further, `TimeoutExpired` may contain partial captured output, while AC-6 requires deliberately returning `stdout == b""`; this needs to be intentional and tested rather than inherited accidentally.
findings.suggestion: Define the bytes helper’s timeout branch concretely: catch `TimeoutExpired`, kill the process if needed, call `communicate()` to reap it, discard any partial output, and return a `CompletedProcess` with `TIMEOUT_RETURNCODE`, `stdout=b""`, and a consistently typed bytes `stderr`. Reuse the existing timeout-cleanup logic if one exists rather than creating a divergent implementation.

findings.finding: The proposed verification command runs only the two new test files. That is insufficient coverage for a refactor of the shared git primitive and does not validate the existing callers whose behavior is explicitly required to remain unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Run the existing `git_base` tests and all tests for the affected sweep/reconciliation modules in addition to the new parity tests; ideally run the project’s normal `shared/tests` suite if it is reasonably scoped. Ensure the new tests assert all acceptance outcomes explicitly: GC count and removal from outbox, `no_drift`, and exactly `folded == 1`.

findings.finding: Centralizing the store decode rule is sound, but changing `read_text_verbatim` from text-file reading with `newline=""` to binary reading plus decode is a behavior-sensitive refactor beyond the immediate git-blob issue. It should preserve current newline and file-read semantics, but the plan asserts this rather than proving it.
findings.suggestion: Add a small characterization test for ordinary UTF-8 content, CRLF/LF preservation, and surrogateescape round-tripping through `read_text_verbatim`. Keep `decode_store_text` narrowly documented as the triage-store byte decode rule, not a general-purpose text decoding API.

findings.finding: No new material injection or authorization risk is introduced if the bytes helper continues to invoke git with an argument list and no shell. The practical security-relevant concern is accidental logging or re-encoding of surrogate-containing text introduced by the new path.
findings.suggestion: Keep the bytes result confined to the three storage-comparison boundaries and avoid routing decoded store text into JSON serialization, subprocess arguments, or logging paths that assume valid Unicode. The proposed scope already largely does this; preserve that boundary discipline.  Overall, decoding git blobs as bytes and applying the existing surrogateescape store decoding rule is the correct, lossless fix and appropriately avoids changing global `run_git` semantics. The plan should be revised to make the shared subprocess refactor’s compatibility and timeout-cleanup guarantees explicit and test them beyond the new regression cases. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: delivered and other spliced the SAME bad byte at DIFFERENT offsets, which does NOT collide under errors='replace' - so a non-injective membership rule would also leave `other` in the outbox and the test would still pass. Verified: collide-under-replace was False. FIXED by varying the byte VALUE at the SAME offset (BAD_BYTE 0xFF vs OTHER_BAD_BYTE 0xFE); the pair now collides under replace and stays distinct under surrogateescape, and the test asserts that precondition inline. Proven in isolation: with the shipped rule is_delivered(other)=False (survives); with a lossy rule is_delivered(other)=True, i.e. the GC would DELETE an undelivered operator finding.

It claimed `binary` selects 'the ONLY difference'. Text mode also performs universal-newline translation (TextIOWrapper, newline=None), so CRLF and lone CR become LF; binary mode does not. Harmless for the three migrated sites (all funnel through normalize_lines/.strip()) and strictly more faithful for a lone CR, but the docstring is what a future migration reads. FIXED: docstring now names both differences and why the store readers are unaffected, plus a new TestNewlineTranslation class pinning bytes-preserves-CRLF vs text-translates-to-LF.

It returns '' for a missing/unstattable path, so a log that vanished under the lock would be reported as 'empty after merge - the header was dropped' instead of read_failed, aiming the operator's repair at the wrong thing. FIXED by reading bytes at the call site and decoding with decode_store_text - keeps the one decode rule while preserving the OSError the handler was written for. This also removes the ledger row-26 caveat at its source.
It explained the ValueError catch via a UnicodeDecodeError that surrogateescape cannot raise. FIXED: rewritten to state the actual reason.
The operator-facing index.lock hint was written out twice and could drift. FIXED: extracted _timeout_message(); one literal remains.
FIXED: core annotated tuple[int, Any, Any] so the two wrappers' narrow public types are the only claims made.
FIXED: renamed to spliceable_status() to name its purpose; the 10 existing status() call sites are untouched.
Correct at review time - F4 had not yet run. FIXED: CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/Fixed/iterate-2026-08-06-gc-decode-parity_001.md written, in plain user-facing language.
